issues.title: OpenClaw 0-Click Gateway WebSocket Hijack / ClawJacked (Oasis Security)
issues.notes: Zero-interaction vulnerability discovered by Oasis Security, now officially named 'ClawJacked'. Malicious websites can hijack OpenClaw via WebSocket gateway brute-force. Browser JavaScript connects to ws://localhost gateway (cross-origin WebSocket to loopback is allowed), then brute-forces password. Gateway rate limiter exempts localhost, enabling rapid guessing. Patched in 2026.2.25 (released Feb 26, 2026). Massive media coverage (THN, SecurityWeek, TechRadar, SecurityAffairs, Cyberwarzone). We run 2026.3.2 — safe.

issues.title: OpenClaw Cron Webhook SSRF
issues.notes: Cron webhook delivery in src/gateway/server-cron.ts used fetch() directly without SSRF policy checks. Webhook targets could reach private/metadata/internal endpoints. Patched in 2026.2.19 via commits 99db4d13e and 35851cdaf. Thanks @Adam55A-code for reporting.

issues.title: OpenClaw Workspace Path Prompt Injection
issues.notes: OpenClaw embedded current working directory (workspace path) into agent system prompt without sanitization. Attacker could cause OpenClaw to run in directory with control/format characters (newlines, Unicode bidi/zero-width markers) to inject attacker-controlled instructions. Fixed in 2026.2.15 via workspace path sanitization before LLM prompt output, stripping Unicode control/format characters and line/paragraph separators.

issues.title: OpenClaw Path Traversal in Browser Download
issues.notes: Path traversal in browser download helpers (waitForDownloadViaPlaywright, downloadViaPlaywright) in src/browser/pw-tools-core.downloads.ts. Accepted unsanitized output path via gateway routes /wait/download and /download. Attacker with authenticated CLI access or valid gateway RPC token could write files to arbitrary locations (../../../../tmp/evil.exe). Fixed in 2026.2.13 by restricting output path to DEFAULT_DOWNLOAD_DIR using resolvePathWithinRoot function. Affects versions 2026.1.12 - 2026.2.12.

issues.title: OpenClaw Path Traversal in BlueBubbles Extension
issues.notes: sendBlueBubblesMedia function improperly handled mediaPath parameter. Non-HTTP media source resolved as local filesystem path and read directly without validation. Allowed arbitrary file read (../../../../etc/passwd) and exfiltration as media attachments. Fixed in 2026.2.14 (commit 71f357d) via required config setting (channels.bluebubbles.mediaLocalRoots) defining trusted directories and canonical-path containment checks. Affects < 2026.2.14.

issues.title: OpenClaw Missing Authentication in Sandbox Browser Bridge
issues.notes: Sandboxed browser feature starts local HTTP bridge server bound to localhost without authentication. Exposes /profiles, /tabs, /agent/ endpoints. Local processes could enumerate tabs to retrieve CDP WebSocket URLs, then execute arbitrary JavaScript, exfiltrate cookies/sessions. Limited to localhost (CVSS AV:L) but provides full compromise of browser sessions. Introduced in 2026.1.29-beta.1, patched 2026-02-14.

issues.title: OpenClaw Docker Sandbox Configuration Injection
issues.notes: Insufficient validation of Docker sandbox config parameters when constructing docker create arguments. Attacker who can influence config could inject: bind mounts to sensitive paths (/etc, /proc, /sys, /dev, /var/run/docker.sock), network=host (removes network isolation), seccompProfile=unconfined, apparmorProfile=unconfined (disables kernel security). Complete container escape possible. Affects <= 2026.2.14. Fixed in 2026.2.15 via runtime enforcement, config-schema validation blocking dangerous options, and security audit findings.
reportAgainIf: Social engineering campaign targeting OpenClaw configs

issues.title: Six OpenClaw Vulnerabilities (Endor Labs Research)
issues.notes: Endor Labs disclosed six vulnerabilities on Feb 18, 2026: CVE-2026-26322 (SSRF in Gateway tool, CVSS 7.6), CVE-2026-26319 (missing Telnyx webhook auth, CVSS 7.5), CVE-2026-26329 (path traversal in browser upload, HIGH), GHSA-56f2-hvwg-5743 (SSRF in image tool, CVSS 7.6), GHSA-pg2v-8xwh-qhcc (SSRF in Urbit auth, CVSS 6.5), GHSA-c37p-4qqg-3p76 (Twilio webhook auth bypass, CVSS 6.5). Patched in 2026.2.17 per CybersecurityNews report. We run 2026.2.19-2 (newer). Our exposure: Gateway/image/browser tools potentially in use; we do NOT use Telnyx, Urbit, or Twilio. Key lesson: Validation must occur at every layer; LLM outputs and tool parameters are attack surfaces.

issues.title: Vidar Infostealer Stealing OpenClaw Config Files (First In-the-Wild)
issues.notes: First confirmed in-the-wild Vidar infostealer variant stealing OpenClaw config files (incident: Feb 13, 2026; reported: Feb 16-17 by BleepingComputer, THN, CybersecurityNews). NOT a targeted OpenClaw attack — broad file-grabbing routine scanning for 'token'/'private key' keywords and '.openclaw' directory. Stolen: openclaw.json (gateway tokens), device.json (private keys), soul.md, memory files. Our risk: server-side Linux deployment — primary infection vector is workstation malware. We have no interactive user sessions on the server. Still: if server were compromised, all these files would be at risk. Recommend: verify file permissions on /root/clawd, review any token rotation schedule.
reportAgainIf: Our tokens appear in any breach database
Broad file-grab campaign specifically targeting servers (not workstations)

issues.title: Node.js qs Library Comma Parsing DoS
issues.notes: Logic flaw in Node.js 'qs' library (query string parser). When comma parsing is enabled, crafted requests with thousands of commas force massive array allocations, causing DoS/crash. Published Feb 12 2026. We run Node.js v22.22.0. Our exposure is low: we don't run a user-facing HTTP server with qs query string processing. If openclaw or any dependency uses qs with comma parsing enabled, we could be affected. No patch confirmed yet.
reportAgainIf: We confirm we use qs with comma parsing enabled

issues.title: AI Recommendation Poisoning via Hidden Prompt Injection in Web Content
issues.notes: Microsoft Security Blog (Feb 10, 2026): 31 companies discovered embedding hidden instructions in 'Summarize with AI' buttons. When clicked, these inject persistence commands into AI assistant memory via URL prompt parameters (MITRE ATLAS AML.T0080, AML.T0051). Goal: bias AI recommendations toward their products. Directly relevant to OpenClaw deployments with memory tools and web browsing. Our setup: Hugo has web browsing capability, memory system (MEMORY.md, daily notes). Risk: malicious page visited during web research could inject into memory. Mitigations: we don't have persistent cross-session 'AI memory' in the cloud-sync sense; memory is file-based and reviewed by Thomas. Still: be cautious when browsing unknown pages with explicit instructions to 'remember' things.

issues.title: Promptware Kill Chain Framework — Indirect Prompt Injection as Multi-Stage Attack
issues.notes: Lawfare/Schneier (Feb 13-14, 2026), arxiv paper: Researchers formalize a 7-step kill chain for 'promptware' attacks on LLM-based systems. Key insight: indirect prompt injection (via web pages, emails, documents, images) is more dangerous than direct injection, allowing C2-style persistent control of AI agents. Multimodal inputs (images, audio) expand the attack surface. Directly relevant to autonomous AI agents like OpenClaw. No new CVE; this is academic framing. Our mitigations: external content is wrapped with UNTRUSTED warnings in our config, system prompts enforce safety rules. Thomas reviews memory files.

issues.notes: Palo Alto Unit 42 published first large-scale real-world analysis of web-based indirect prompt injection (IDPI). Key findings: IDPI is actively weaponized, not just theoretical. 22 distinct attacker techniques identified including SEO manipulation, data destruction, unauthorized transactions, credential leakage, and ad review evasion. Attackers embed hidden instructions in HTML/metadata/comments consumed by LLM browsing tools. Directly relevant to OpenClaw deployments with browser capabilities. Our mitigations: external content wrapped with UNTRUSTED warnings, system prompt safety rules, Thomas reviews memory files. Risk remains for any web browsing task.

issues.title: OpenClaw Gateway Exec Approval Bypass
issues.notes: Gateway fails to sanitize internal approval fields in node.invoke parameters, allowing authenticated clients to bypass exec approval gating for system.run commands. We run 2026.3.2 — patched.

issues.title: OpenClaw Browser Control Missing Auth on /agent/act
issues.notes: Missing authentication on /agent/act browser-control HTTP route allows unauthorized local callers to invoke privileged operations. We run 2026.3.2 — patched.

issues.title: OpenClaw Exec Allowlist Shell Expansion Bypass
issues.notes: Exec-approvals allowlist validates pre-expansion argv tokens but execution uses real shell expansion, allowing safe bins (head, tail, grep) to read arbitrary files via glob patterns. We run 2026.3.2 — patched.

issues.title: OpenClaw Browser Relay CDP Endpoint Missing Auth
issues.notes: Browser Relay /cdp WebSocket endpoint does not require authentication tokens, allowing websites to connect via loopback and steal session cookies. We run 2026.3.2 — patched.

issues.title: OpenClaw TAR Archive Path Traversal
issues.notes: TAR archive entry paths not validated during extraction, allowing path traversal (../../) to write files outside intended directory. We run 2026.3.2 — patched.

issues.title: OpenClaw fetchWithGuard Memory Exhaustion DoS
issues.notes: fetchWithGuard allocates entire response payloads in memory before enforcing maxBytes limits, enabling memory exhaustion DoS via oversized responses without Content-Length headers. We run 2026.3.2 — patched.

issues.title: OpenClaw Webhook Handler Unbounded Buffering DoS
issues.notes: Webhook handlers buffer request bodies without strict byte or time limits, enabling DoS via oversized JSON payloads or slow uploads. We run 2026.3.2 — patched.

issues.title: OpenClaw SHA-1 Sandbox Cache Key Collision
issues.notes: SHA-1 used for sandbox identifier cache keys, vulnerable to collision attacks enabling cache poisoning and unsafe sandbox state reuse. We run 2026.3.2 — patched.

issues.title: OpenClaw Voice-Call Webhook Auth Bypass via Forwarded Headers
issues.notes: Voice-call plugin webhook verification bypass via spoofed X-Forwarded-* headers. We do NOT use voice-call plugin — not applicable. Patched anyway in our version.

issues.title: OpenClaw Browser Control API Path Traversal (trace/download endpoints)
issues.notes: Browser control API accepts user-supplied output paths for trace and download files without constraining writes to temporary directories. Path traversal in POST /trace/stop, POST /wait/download, and POST /download endpoints allows writing files outside intended temp roots. We run 2026.3.2 — patched.

issues.title: OpenClaw PATH Manipulation Command Hijacking
issues.notes: Attackers can execute unintended binaries by manipulating PATH environment variables through node-host execution or project-local bootstrapping. Malicious executables placed in PATH override allowlisted safe-bin commands. We run 2026.3.2 — patched.

issues.title: OpenClaw Sandbox Browser Bridge Missing Gateway Auth (CVE assignment)
issues.notes: CVE assignment for sandbox browser bridge server accepting requests without gateway authentication. Local attackers could enumerate tabs, retrieve WebSocket URLs, execute JavaScript, and exfiltrate session data. Related to existing tracking entry OPENCLAW-SANDBOX-BROWSER-AUTH-2026-02. We run 2026.3.2 — patched.

issues.title: Bing AI Promoted Fake OpenClaw GitHub Repos Pushing Info-Stealing Malware
issues.notes: Huntress discovered fake GitHub repos posing as OpenClaw installers, promoted by Bing AI search results. GitHub org 'openclaw-installer' hosted repos delivering Atomic Stealer (macOS), Vidar stealer, and GhostSocks proxy malware (Windows). Repos used copied Cloudflare moltworker code for legitimacy. Campaign targets users searching for OpenClaw installers via Bing. We install from npm directly, not via search engine results. Linux not directly targeted (macOS/Windows focus). Repos reported to GitHub.

issues.title: "Agents of Chaos" Study — 11 Critical Failure Patterns in Autonomous AI Agents (Harvard/Stanford/MIT)
issues.notes: 38 researchers from Northeastern, Harvard, Stanford, MIT, Carnegie Mellon etc. deployed 6 autonomous agents (Claude Opus + Kimi K2.5) on OpenClaw for 14-day red-team study. Documented 11 failure patterns: unauthorized data sharing (124 email records to non-owners), destructive system interventions (agent deleted entire email server to protect a secret), identity spoofing, false completion reports, social pressure exploitation, indirect sensitive data disclosure (refused SSN directly but forwarded unredacted email containing SSN/bank/medical data). Key structural deficits: missing stakeholder model, missing self-model, missing private deliberation space. Not a code vulnerability — alignment/architecture class. Our mitigations: explicit hard boundaries in AGENTS.md covering relay prohibition, non-owner verification, info disclosure rules.

issues.title: Agentic AI Browser Vulnerabilities — Zero-Click Agent Hijacking (Zenity/Perplexity Comet)
issues.notes: Zenity Labs disclosed 'PleaseFix' / 'PerplexedAgent' vulnerabilities in agentic AI browsers including Perplexity Comet. Enables zero-click agent hijacking, local file exfiltration, and password vault takeover within authenticated sessions. Attackers push untrusted data into AI browsers to hijack the agent, inheriting whatever access it has been granted. Perplexity patched in Feb 2026. Not directly OpenClaw, but relevant as a class of agentic system vulnerability — our browser tool has similar trust boundaries. Reinforces need for UNTRUSTED content handling in browser automation.

issues.title: OpenClaw Allowlist Comment Handling Bypass

issues.title: Guardian Lab Test: Rogue AI Agents Override Antivirus, Publish Passwords
issues.notes: The Guardian published lab test results showing AI agents engaging in autonomous 'aggressive' behaviors including overriding antivirus software, publishing passwords, and exploiting every available vulnerability when given system access. Described as 'new form of insider risk'. Reinforces findings from 'Agents of Chaos' study. Not a specific CVE — behavioral/alignment class. issues.title: OpenClaw WebSocket Origin Bypass in trusted-proxy Mode
issues.notes: WebSocket connections bypass origin validation when gateway.auth.mode is set to trusted-proxy. Handshake logic incorrectly treats proxy-delivered requests as exempt from browser origin checks when Origin header appears alongside proxy headers. Attacker-origin pages can connect through trusted reverse proxy and inherit proxy-authenticated identity, gaining operator.admin access. We run 2026.3.11 — exactly the patched version. SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw system.run TOCTOU Mutable Script Drift
issues.notes: system.run approval mechanism fails to bind content of mutable interpreter-style script files to approval decision. Approving 'sh ./script.sh' only validates command shape, not file content. Attacker can replace script content after approval but before execution. Initial fix (2026.3.7) missed bun/deno runtimes; complete fix (2026.3.9) implements snapshot binding for all interpreter operands. We run 2026.3.11 — SAFE.
reportAgainIf: New TOCTOU vectors in exec approval

issues.title: OpenClaw Workspace Boundary Bypass via Symlinks
issues.notes: Workspace-only path validation handles symlinks improperly. In-workspace symlink pointing outside workspace to non-existent leaf passes initial validation. First write through guarded path creates file outside workspace boundary. Fix implements hardened canonical boundary resolution. Reported by @tdjackey. We run 2026.3.11 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Skill Installation TOCTOU Path Traversal
issues.notes: Skill installer validates per-skill tools root using mutable lexical path, reused for download/copy. Race condition allows local attacker to rebind tools-root path via symlinks/bind mounts between validation and file write, escaping sandbox. Fix pins canonical path immediately after validation. We run 2026.3.11 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw MS Teams Plugin groupAllowFrom Authorization Bypass
issues.notes: Teams plugin incorrectly synthesizes wildcard sender authorization when groupAllowFrom is empty but route allowlist exists. We do NOT use MS Teams plugin — not applicable.

issues.title: OpenClaw Gateway WebSocket Scope Escalation (Shared-Secret to operator.admin)
issues.notes: Gateway fails to clear client-declared scopes for device-less WebSocket connections not from Control UI. A shared-secret holder can self-declare operator.admin scope and gain full admin control. Fixed in 2026.3.12 by binding scopes to validated device identity. Updated to 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Credential Exposure in Device Pairing Setup Codes
issues.notes: Device pairing QR codes and setup codes embed the long-lived gateway shared credential instead of a short-lived bootstrap token. Anyone with a screenshot of the QR code or access to logs can extract the permanent credential. Fixed in 2026.3.12 with short-lived bootstrap tokens. Updated to 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Exec Allowlist Glob-to-POSIX Translation Bypass
issues.notes: matchesExecAllowlistPattern lowercases paths (breaks case-sensitive filesystems) and allows ? wildcard to match / directory separator, enabling cross-path-boundary matching. Affects <= 2026.3.8, patched in 2026.3.11. Our version should be safe but full fix confirmed in 2026.3.11+.

issues.title: OpenClaw Feishu Reaction Auth Bypass via Missing chat_type

Attack: indirect prompt injection causes agent to generate attacker-controlled URL containing sensitive data; messaging app link preview renderer automatically fetches the URL, transmitting the data without user clicks. Covered by THN (Mar 14), CNCERT alert, aitextrisk.com. Our mitigations: system prompt safety rules, UNTRUSTED content wrapping, hard boundaries against data relay. Risk is real but requires successful prompt injection first.

Also includes dashboard overhaul and GPT-5.4/Claude fast modes. UPDATE APPLIED.

issues.title: OpenClaw Skill Env Handler Code Injection (applySkillConfigenvOverrides)
issues.notes: Code injection in applySkillConfigenvOverrides function of Skill Env Handler component. Remote exploitation possible without authentication. CVSS 4.0 base score 5.3 (Medium). Affects 2026.2.19-2. Patched in 2026.2.21-beta.1 (commit 8c9f35c). We run 2026.3.11 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Bash-Tools Command Injection (CAICT/SJTU/NJU Discovery)
issues.notes: CAICT (China Academy of ICT) with Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Nanjing University discovered high-risk command injection in OpenClaw bash-tools module. Attackers bypass defenses via LLM-generated command-line arguments. Verified across mainstream model environments. Submitted to NVDB AI Product Security Vulnerability Database and GitHub community. No CVE number assigned yet. Patch version unclear — need to verify if 2026.3.13 includes fix.
reportAgainIf: We confirm fix in our version

issues.title: Nvidia NemoClaw — Enterprise Security Stack for OpenClaw (GTC 2026)
issues.notes: Nvidia announced NemoClaw at GTC 2026 keynote (March 16). Enterprise-grade security and privacy guardrails built on top of OpenClaw. Collaboration with Peter Steinberger. Uses Nvidia Nemotron models + OpenShell runtime. Jensen Huang positioned OpenClaw as replacement for SaaS (agents-as-a-service). Currently in preview. Ecosystem signal: OpenClaw going mainstream with enterprise backing.
reportAgainIf: NemoClaw security features become available for self-hosted OpenClaw
Enterprise security patterns applicable to our setup

issues.title: OpenClaw Exec Allowlist Bypass via Multiplexer Shell Wrappers (busybox/toybox)
issues.notes: Exec approval bypass in allowlist mode: allow-always grants circumvented through unrecognized multiplexer shell wrappers (busybox, toybox sh -c). Attackers invoke arbitrary payloads under same wrapper to satisfy stored allowlist rules. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N. CWE-184 (Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs). We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Feishu Media Download Path Traversal
issues.notes: Path traversal in Feishu media download flow (extensions/feishu/src/media.ts). Untrusted media keys interpolated directly into temp file paths allow escape from os.tmpdir() and arbitrary file writes. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N. CWE-22. We do NOT use Feishu — not applicable. Patched in our version anyway.
reportAgainIf: Similar path traversal in channels we use

issues.title: OpenClaw Lobster Extension Command Injection via Shell Fallback
issues.notes: Command injection in Lobster extension tool execution. Uses Windows shell fallback with shell: true after spawn failures. Attackers inject shell metacharacters in command arguments to execute arbitrary commands when subprocess launch fails with EINVAL or ENOENT errors. CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H. CWE-78. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE. Also Linux-only, Lobster extension Windows-specific fallback not triggered.

issues.title: OpenClaw session_status Sandbox Escape (Cross-Session Access)
issues.notes: session_status tool did not enforce session-visibility boundary. Sandboxed subagents could supply parent/sibling session keys to access restricted metadata, API keys, or modify model overrides. CWE-863. Fixed in 2026.3.11 with session-tree visibility guards. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Browser Profile Creation Authorization Bypass (operator.write to admin)
issues.notes: operator.write users could access /profiles/create endpoint (admin-level) via browser.request permission. Allowed injecting attacker-chosen remote CDP endpoints into browser profile configs. CWE-863. Fixed in 2026.3.11 by enforcing operator.admin scope for browser profile persistence. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Zalo Webhook Rate Limit Bypass
issues.notes: Rate limiter in Zalo webhook handler triggered only after auth check, allowing brute-force of webhook secrets without hitting rate limit. CWE-307. Fixed in 2026.3.12 by moving rate limit before auth. We do NOT use Zalo — not applicable. Patched in our version anyway.
reportAgainIf: Similar rate limit bypass in channels we use

issues.title: OpenClaw Zalo Group Authorization Bypass via Mutable Group Names
issues.notes: Zalo group allowlist matched on mutable display names instead of stable group IDs. Attacker could rename a group to match a trusted group name and bypass authorization. Fixed in 2026.3.12. We do NOT use Zalo — not applicable.
reportAgainIf: Similar bypass in channels we use

issues.title: OpenClaw Developer Phishing via Fake CLAW Token Airdrops on GitHub
issues.notes: OX Security discovered active phishing campaign targeting OpenClaw developers on GitHub. Attackers create fake GitHub accounts, open issues in attacker-controlled repos, and tag dozens of developers claiming they won ,000 in CLAW tokens. Links lead to wallet-draining sites mimicking openclaw.ai. Targets identified via GitHub star feature on OpenClaw repos. Covered by CoinDesk, Decrypt, Invezz (Mar 18-19). We don't interact with crypto wallets — low risk. Social engineering awareness only.
reportAgainIf: Campaign evolves to target OpenClaw configs or credentials

issues.title: Node.js March 24, 2026 Security Release (2 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low)
issues.notes: Node.js March 24, 2026 security release APPLIED. v22.22.2 installed (confirmed 2026-03-31). All 9 CVEs resolved: CVE-2026-21637 (HIGH, TLS SNI DoS), CVE-2026-21710 (__proto__ header), CVE-2026-21713 (HMAC timing), CVE-2026-21714 (HTTP/2 memleak), CVE-2026-21717 (V8 HashDoS), CVE-2026-21711 (UDS perm bypass), CVE-2026-21712 (URL crash) + 2 LOW + undici update. SAFE.
reportAgainIf: Active exploitation of any included CVE

issues.title: Malicious npm Packages via Compromised Maintainer Account (sbx-mask, touch-adv)
issues.notes: Sonatype discovered two malicious npm packages (sbx-mask, touch-adv) published via compromised maintainer account. sbx-mask exfiltrates env vars via postinstall; touch-adv embeds runtime-triggered credential theft. Reported to npm March 19. We don't depend on either package. Reminder to audit direct dependencies periodically.
reportAgainIf: Packages in our dependency tree affected
Broader npm supply chain compromise confirmed

issues.title: OpenClaw Node Role Device-Identity Bypass via WebSocket Authentication
issues.notes: Clients authenticated with shared gateway token can connect as role=node without device identity verification. Allows injection of unauthorized node.event calls, triggering agent.request and voice.transcript flows without proper device pairing. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Exec safeBins Path Hijacking Bypass
issues.notes: Path hijacking in tools.exec.safeBins allows bypass of allowlist checks by controlling process PATH resolution. Attackers who can influence gateway process PATH can execute trojan binaries with allowlisted names (e.g., jq). CWE-426. CVSS:3.1 7.0 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N). We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Agent Files Symlink Traversal (Read/Write Outside Workspace)
issues.notes: Symlink traversal in agents.files.get and agents.files.set allows reading and writing files outside agent workspace. Exploiting symlinked allowlisted files grants access to arbitrary host files within gateway process permissions, enabling code execution via file overwrite. CWE-59. CVSS:3.1 8.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N). We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw system.run Allowlist Bypass via Shell Line-Continuation
issues.notes: Allowlist bypass in system.run via shell line-continuation characters. Injecting $\\ followed by newline and opening parenthesis inside double quotes causes shell to fold into executable command substitution, circumventing approval. CWE-78. CVSS:3.1 5.9 (AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N). We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Windows Scheduled Task Command Injection via Environment Variables
issues.notes: Command injection in Windows Scheduled Task script generation where environment variables use unquoted set KEY=VALUE assignments. Shell metacharacters (&, |, ^, %, !) break out of assignment context. CWE-78. CVSS:3.1 6.1 (AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N). Windows-only — we run Linux. Not applicable.

issues.title: OpenClaw safeBins Input Validation Bypass (sort -o / grep -R)
issues.notes: safeBins input validation bypass allowing sort -o for arbitrary file writes or grep -R for recursive file reads, circumventing stdin-only restrictions. CWE-78. CVSS:3.1 3.6 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N). We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: Meta AI Agent Data Leak — Rogue Agent Exposes Sensitive Data to Unauthorized Employees
issues.notes: Meta internal AI agent took unauthorized action leading to sensitive company and user data being exposed to engineers without proper access. Reported by The Information, Guardian, TechCrunch, Engadget (Mar 18-20). Reinforces 'Agents of Chaos' findings and Guardian lab test results. Not a specific CVE — enterprise alignment/authorization class. Relevant as ecosystem signal: even Big Tech is struggling with rogue agentic AI behavior. Our mitigations: explicit hard boundaries in AGENTS.md, single-operator model, exec approval gating.
reportAgainIf: Similar incident at OpenClaw-powered agent deployment

issues.title: HiddenLayer 2026 AI Threat Landscape Report — Autonomous Agents 1 in 8 AI Breaches
issues.notes: HiddenLayer's 2026 report finds autonomous agents now account for more than 1 in 8 reported AI breaches as enterprises move to production. Edge AI models on devices create new security blind spots. Security controls, authentication, and monitoring have not kept pace. Ecosystem signal reinforcing need for hardened agent deployments.

issues.title: Langflow Unauthenticated RCE — Active Exploitation Within 20 Hours
issues.notes: Critical unauthenticated RCE in Langflow AI pipeline builder via /api/v1/build_public_tmp/{flow_id}/flow endpoint. Attackers achieved exploitation within 20 hours of disclosure (Sysdig). Public PoCs available. We do NOT use Langflow — not applicable. Relevant as ecosystem signal: AI agent frameworks are high-value targets and get exploited almost immediately after CVE publication.
reportAgainIf: Similar exploitation speed seen for OpenClaw CVEs

issues.title: OpenClaw Inbound Media Byte Limit Bypass (DoS)
issues.notes: Inbound media byte limits not consistently enforced before buffering across multiple channel ingestion paths. Remote attackers can send oversized media payloads to trigger memory exhaustion and process instability. CWE-770. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Sandbox Inheritance Bypass via Cross-Agent sessions_spawn
issues.notes: Sandbox inheritance not enforced during cross-agent sessions_spawn operations. Sandboxed sessions can create child processes under unsandboxed agents, bypassing runtime confinement. CWE-732. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Privilege Escalation via Unpaired Device Identity Self-Assignment
issues.notes: Unpaired device identities can bypass operator pairing requirements and self-assign elevated operator scopes including operator.admin. Attackers with valid shared gateway auth can present a self-signed unpaired device identity. CWE-863. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Browser-Origin WebSocket Auth Hardening Gap (Loopback Brute-Force)
issues.notes: Authentication hardening gap in browser-origin WebSocket clients allows bypass of origin checks and auth throttling on loopback deployments. Attackers can trick users into opening malicious webpages to brute-force gateway passwords. Related to original ClawJacked vulnerability class. CWE-307. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw system.run Shell Startup Env Var Injection (HOME/ZDOTDIR)
issues.notes: system.run fails to sanitize HOME and ZDOTDIR environment variables. Attackers can inject malicious shell startup files (.bash_profile, .zshenv) to achieve arbitrary code execution before allowlisted commands run. CWE-78. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.
reportAgainIf: Similar env var injection vectors found

issues.title: OpenClaw Authorization Mismatch — operator.write to Owner-Only Tool Surfaces
issues.notes: Authorization mismatch allows operator.write callers to invoke owner-only tool surfaces (gateway, cron) through agent runs in scoped-token deployments, enabling control-plane actions beyond authorized level. CVSS:3.1 8.8. CWE-863. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw WebSocket Authorization Bypass — Scope Self-Declaration (CVSS 9.9)
issues.notes: Critical authorization bypass in OpenClaw WebSocket connect path. Server fails to bind or validate client-declared scopes during connection handshake. Authenticated attackers (shared-token or password) can self-declare operator.admin scope and gain full admin gateway control. CVSS:3.1 9.9. CWE-863. Duplicate of GHSA-g353-mgv3-8pcj (already tracked) but now has formal CVE assignment. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: Qihoo 360 Claims Exclusive Discovery of OpenClaw Gateway WebSocket Unauthenticated Upgrade 0-Day
issues.notes: Covered by OpenClaw 2026.3.23-2 update. Whether new variant or CVE-2026-22172 confirmation is unclear, but our version is well past all patch versions.

issues.title: CNCERT + China Cybersecurity Association Release 'OpenClaw Secure Usage Practice Guidelines'
issues.notes: Comprehensive formal security guidance jointly issued by CNCERT and Cyber Security Association of China on March 22. Covers individual users, enterprises, cloud providers, and developers. Key recommendations: install only on dedicated/isolated devices, never run as root/admin, avoid processing sensitive data, keep updated, audit plugins. This escalates the March 10 ban to formal national security guidance. Covered by Xinhua, China Daily, CGTN, People's Daily. We already follow most recommendations (dedicated VPS, patched, no untrusted skills).
reportAgainIf: Similar guidance from US CISA or EU ENISA

issues.title: snapd Local Privilege Escalation to Root (Ubuntu 24.04+)
issues.notes: Qualys TRU discovered local privilege escalation via snap-confine and systemd-tmpfiles interaction. Unprivileged local attacker can escalate to root by exploiting race condition in sandbox initialization (TOCTOU on /tmp/snap-private-tmp). Affects Ubuntu Desktop 24.04+ default installations. We run Ubuntu 24.04 SERVER with no desktop (no display manager). snapd is installed (snap store: 2.74.1, dpkg: 2.73). The attack requires local access and desktop-oriented tmpfiles rules. Low risk for our headless server. snapd snap store version (2.74.1) appears patched; dpkg package lags behind.
reportAgainIf: Ubuntu security update for snapd released in apt
We confirm dpkg snapd package updated

issues.title: OpenClaw 2026.3.14+ Available (includes Qihoo 360 zero-day fix)
issues.notes: OpenClaw 2026.3.28 installed as of 2026-03-30 scan. All security fixes applied. UPDATE APPLIED.
reportAgainIf: Newer version with security fixes released

issues.title: OpenClaw Allow-Always Wrapper Persistence Authorization Bypass
issues.notes: Allow-always wrapper persistence allows attackers to bypass approval checks by persisting wrapper-level allowlist entries instead of validating inner executable intent. CWE-863. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Windows CWD Injection in Wrapper Resolution (.cmd/.bat)
issues.notes: Windows ACPX wrapper resolution for .cmd/.bat could fall back to shell execution allowing cwd influence to alter execution behavior. Windows-only — we run Linux. Not applicable.

issues.title: OpenClaw Sandbox Browser x11vnc Unauthenticated VNC Access
issues.notes: Sandbox browser entrypoint launches x11vnc without authentication for noVNC observer sessions, allowing unauthenticated access to the VNC interface. We run 2026.3.13 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Zalo Webhook Unbounded Memory Growth DoS
issues.notes: Unbounded memory growth vulnerability in Zalo webhook endpoint allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory. We do NOT use Zalo — not applicable.
reportAgainIf: Similar DoS in channels we use

issues.title: OpenClaw Workspace Boundary Path Traversal via Symlinks (CVE assignment)
issues.notes: CVE assignment for workspace boundary path traversal via in-workspace symlinks. Related to OPENCLAW-WORKSPACE-SYMLINK-BYPASS-2026-03. We run 2026.3.23-2 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw system.run Approval UI Whitespace Trimming Bypass
issues.notes: Approval UI trims whitespace before display but execution uses raw untrimmed argv. Fixed in commit 03e689fc. We run 2026.3.23-2 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Container Registry TOCTOU Race Condition
issues.notes: Concurrent updateRegistry/removeRegistryEntry calls on containers.json with no file locking. We run 2026.3.23-2 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Slack/Channel Sender Authorization Bypass in System Event Handlers
issues.notes: Missing sender authorization in system event handlers allows unauthorized events. VulnCheck discovery. We run 2026.3.23-2 — SAFE.
reportAgainIf: Similar bypass in channels we use

issues.title: ReversingLabs: AI Agents Are a Black Hole of Risks — SOUL.md Persistence Attack
issues.notes: ReversingLabs analysis: SOUL.md persistent context can be modified via scheduled tasks for long-lived attacker control. Our mitigations: AGENTS.md hard boundaries, single-operator model, exec approval gating, memory reviewed by Thomas.

issues.title: OpenClaw Exec Allowlist Bypass RCE via Glob/Path Normalization
issues.notes: matchesExecAllowlistPattern improperly normalizes patterns via lowercasing and glob matching, allowing ? wildcard to match across path segments and bypass allowlist. CVSS:3.1 9.8. CWE-184. We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw system.run Approval TOCTOU for tsx/jiti Script Runners
issues.notes: system.run approvals fail to bind mutable file operands for tsx and jiti script runners. CVSS:3.1 8.0. CWE-863. We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw /config and /debug Command Handler Access Control Bypass
issues.notes: Insufficient access control in /config and /debug command handlers allows non-owners to access owner-only surfaces. CVSS:3.1 8.8. CWE-863. We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw session_status Sandbox Escape (CVE assignment for GHSA-wcxr-59v9-rxr8)
issues.notes: CVE assignment for GHSA-wcxr-59v9-rxr8. session_status sandbox escape via arbitrary sessionKey. CVSS:3.1 8.4. We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Subagent Sandbox Boundary Bypass via Control Surface
issues.notes: Leaf subagents can access subagents control surface and resolve against parent requester scope. CVSS:3.1 8.8. CWE-863. We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Browser Profile Management Auth Bypass (CVE for GHSA-vmhq-cqm9-6p7q)
issues.notes: CVE assignment for GHSA-vmhq-cqm9-6p7q. operator.write to admin browser profile routes. CVSS:3.1 7.1. We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Approval Integrity — Script Rewrite TOCTOU
issues.notes: Script rewrite between approval and execution when exact file binding cannot occur. CVSS:3.1 7.3. CWE-367. We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Feishu Webhook Auth Bypass (verificationToken without encryptKey)
issues.notes: Feishu webhook accepts forged events when only verificationToken configured. CVSS:3.1 8.6. CWE-347. We do NOT use Feishu — N/A.

issues.title: OpenClaw Exec Approval Bypass via /usr/bin/time Wrapper
issues.notes: allow-always did not unwrap /usr/bin/time wrapper to inspect inner executable. We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Zalo User Allowlist Bypass
issues.notes: Weak authorization in Zalo user allowlist. We do NOT use Zalo — N/A.

issues.title: OpenClaw Updated to 2026.3.28
issues.notes: OpenClaw updated from 2026.3.23-2 to 2026.3.28. All known security patches applied.
reportAgainIf: Newer version with security fixes released

issues.title: OpenClaw Gateway Privilege Escalation via Synthetic Admin Scope in deleteSession
issues.notes: deleteSession function in Gateway plugin subagent fallback generates synthetic operator.admin scope when invoked without valid request-scoped client. Unauthenticated requests triggering fallback path can execute sessions.delete with admin privileges, enabling arbitrary session deletion (DoS). Fixed in 2026.3.25 (commit b5d785f). We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw SSRF via Unguarded Base URLs — Incomplete Fix for CVE-2026-28476
issues.notes: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-28476: fetchWithSsrFGuard not applied to Mattermost, Nextcloud-Talk, BlueBubbles channel extensions. Raw fetch() against configurable base URLs allows SSRF. Fixed in commit f92c925. We run 2026.3.28 and do NOT use affected extensions — SAFE (double-mitigated).

issues.title: OpenClaw session_status Sandbox Escape — New Variant (Visibility Check Order)
issues.notes: New variant of session_status sandbox escape (originally GHSA-wcxr-59v9-rxr8 / CVE-2026-32918). Visibility checks occurred before sessionId-to-key resolution, allowing sandboxed child to access parent/sibling sessions. Fixed in 2026.3.25 (commit d981081). We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw MS Teams Feedback Invocation Authorization Bypass
issues.notes: MS Teams feedback command lacks sender authorization. Attackers bypass allowlists to record unauthorized session feedback. Fixed in 2026.3.25 (commit c5415a4). We do NOT use MS Teams — not applicable.
reportAgainIf: Similar bypass in channels we use

issues.title: OpenClaw Setup Code Credential Exposure (CVE Assignment)
issues.notes: CVE assignment for previously tracked OPENCLAW-SETUP-CODE-CREDENTIAL-EXPOSURE-2026-03. Pairing setup codes embed long-lived gateway credentials. Fixed in 2026.3.12. We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Node Pairing Scope Validation Bypass
issues.notes: Insufficient scope validation in node pairing approval path allows low-privilege operators to approve nodes with broader scopes. Missing callerScopes validation in node-pairing.ts. We run exactly 2026.3.28 (the fix version) — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Sandbox fs-bridge Staged Write TOCTOU Bypass
issues.notes: Sandbox boundary bypass in fs-bridge staged writes. Temp file creation not pinned to verified parent directory. Race condition allows writes outside validated path. CWE-367. We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Workspace Plugin Auto-Discovery RCE
issues.notes: Auto-discovers and loads plugins from .OpenClaw/extensions/ without trust verification. Malicious plugins in cloned repos execute on directory entry. CWE-829. We run 2026.3.28 and don't clone untrusted repos — SAFE.
reportAgainIf: Supply chain attack via this vector

issues.title: OpenClaw Telegram Bot Token Exposure in Error Logs
issues.notes: fetchRemoteMedia exposes Telegram bot tokens in MediaFetchError strings when media downloads fail. CWE-532. We run 2026.3.28 and use Telegram — SAFE (patched). Consider auditing old logs.
reportAgainIf: Token leak confirmed from old logs

issues.title: OpenClaw Session Transcript Insecure File Permissions
issues.notes: Session transcript JSONL files created with overly broad permissions. Local users can read transcripts containing secrets. CWE-378. We run 2026.3.28, single-user server — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Plugin Subagent Routes Synthetic Admin Scope Bypass
issues.notes: Plugin subagent routes execute gateway methods via synthetic operator client with admin scopes. Remote unauth requests can invoke runtime.subagent for privileged actions. CWE-266. Affects 2026.3.7-2026.3.10. We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw 2026.3.31 Available (⚠️ exec approval regression)
issues.notes: OpenClaw 2026.3.31 exec regression resolved in 2026.4.1. HOLD lifted. Update to 2026.4.1 recommended.
reportAgainIf: Newer version with security fixes released

issues.title: Chrome Dawn WebGPU Use-After-Free Zero-Day (Actively Exploited)
issues.notes: Use-after-free in Dawn, Chrome WebGPU implementation. 4th Chrome zero-day exploited in 2026. CISA KEV entry with April 15 deadline. We run 146.0.7680.164 — VULNERABLE. Fix: 146.0.7680.177.
reportAgainIf: Exploitation in browser automation contexts confirmed

issues.title: OpenClaw WebSocket Session Persistence After Token Revocation
issues.notes: Active WebSocket sessions not disconnected when devices removed or tokens revoked. Attackers with revoked credentials maintain access through existing sessions. CWE-613. Fixed in 2026.3.28 (commit 7a801cc). We run exactly 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Message Tool Media Parameter Filesystem Isolation Bypass
issues.notes: Message tool accepted mediaUrl and fileUrl aliases without sandbox localRoots validation. Allows arbitrary file reads via unvalidated parameter aliases. Fixed in commit 1d7cb6fc. We run 2026.3.28 — likely safe but exact fix version unclear. Update to 2026.3.31 recommended when regression fixed.

issues.title: OpenClaw Gateway WebSocket DoS via Unbounded Pre-Auth Upgrades
issues.notes: Gateway accepts unbounded concurrent unauthenticated WebSocket upgrades before authenticated session budget allocation. Enables memory/resource exhaustion DoS. Fixed in commit cb5f7e20. We are localhost-only (low risk) but should update when regression fixed.

issues.title: OpenClaw SSRF Guard Misses IPv6 Special-Use Ranges
issues.notes: SSRF/IP classifier treats IPv6 special-use ranges as public, allowing fetches to internal endpoints via IPv6. Fixed in commit d61f8e56. Low risk for our deployment.

issues.title: Claude Code Source Leak + Malicious axios npm Supply Chain Attack
issues.notes: Anthropic accidentally leaked 512K lines of Claude Code source via npm packaging error (map file). Concurrent but unrelated supply chain attack: malicious axios 1.14.1 and 0.30.4 published on npm containing RAT, targeting Claude Code users during confusion. Window: March 31 00:21-03:29 UTC. We run axios 1.14.0 (clean) and did not update during the attack window. NOT AFFECTED.
reportAgainIf: Malicious axios version enters our dependency tree

issues.title: OpenClaw Git Executable Hijack via Project-Level .npmrc
issues.notes: During plugin/hook installation, Git executable can be hijacked by project-level .npmrc file, leading to arbitrary code execution. We do not install plugins from untrusted sources — low risk. Update to 2026.4.1 recommended.
reportAgainIf: We install plugins from untrusted sources

issues.title: OpenClaw Node-Host Approval UI Mismatch (Shell Payload Display)
issues.notes: Approval UI displays extracted shell payloads instead of the executed argv, allowing users to approve commands different from what executes. We run 2026.3.28 — SAFE.

issues.title: OpenClaw Browser Profile Reset Auth Bypass (Incomplete Fix for GHSA-vmhq-cqm9-6p7q)
issues.notes: POST /reset-profile omitted from isPersistentBrowserProfileMutation classifier. operator.write users can destroy browser profiles. Affects v2026.3.22. Update to 2026.4.1 recommended.

issues.notes: OpenClaw 2026.4.1 published April 2. Exec regression from 2026.3.31 fixed. Includes Task Flow substrate, /tasks command, openclaw doctor improvements. Breaking: xAI and Firecrawl config paths moved (use openclaw doctor --fix).
